newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes slide with WTI, extra crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes slide with WTI, extra crude.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light and heavey crude prices slid Monday, weighed by a combination of ample PADD 5 supplies and pressure from falling futures markets, traders said.
No cargoes of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude traded Monday, with the grade's leading seller, BP, out of the market.
Buyers of ANS talked differentials of $1.60 a barrel under April West Texas Intermediate, and saw the $1.10 cargo done February 11 as too high with Gulf sour grades falling.
No buyers bid for spot March barrels of ANS.
Meanwhile, NYMEX prices for April WTI dropped 68 cents a barrel to $20.71 on report of warmer weather in the U.S. Northeast.
Outright prices for ANS were talked $19.80/20.00 a barrel, down 80 cents from late Friday.
IPL Energy Inc, a major Canadian pipeline operator, said Monday they would not apportion crude oil shipments on their line from Hardisty, Alberta, to the mid-Western U.S..
Buyers saw the lack of apportionment trimming exports to the West Coast, and helping to keep ANS discounts tight.
West Coast refiners often run light Canadian crudes instead of ANS
Traders said Line 63 prices stood at postings plus $0.95 - $1.05, with the WTI-based market assessed at minus $1.95 to minus $1.85 under WTI.

Kern River heavy crude fell as most California major oil companies dropped their postings 75 cents a barrel. Outright prices ranged 13.84/14.04 a barrel, traders said, with rumors that an extra 5,000 to 10,000 bpd of heavies were moving east over the All-American pipeline.
